name: Mammoth Manufacturing
old_description: For over 30 years, Mammoth Manufacturing has been the go-to choice for sewing and manufacturing projects in the Eugene area. With our vast experience and expertise, we are fully equipped to handle projects of any size and complexity. From small-scale custom orders to large-scale manufacturing ventures, Mammoth Manufacturing is here to meet your every need.
about:
Mammoth Manufacturing operates from Eugene, Oregon, where it was established in 1996 by owner Ken Rodgers. Rodgers began producing sewn goods in 1984, crafting rafting D-rings in his garage after failing to find suitable options on the market. That venture evolved into Mammoth Manufacturing and its sister brand Whitewater Designs, growing to a team of up to 10 employees.

The shop provides contract sewing and production services, specializing in techniques such as industrial sewing (single- and double-needle), bar tacking, pattern tacking, five-thread surging, die cutting, hot-knife cutting, kick-press grommet and hole punching, and high-frequency RF welding. A climate-controlled, pest-free warehouse supports material storage and logistics, allowing the company to ship anything from single units to 1,000-unit runs.

The company focuses on the outdoor industry, working with materials including Cordura, vinyl, webbing, nylon fabric, mesh, rope, and Hypalon. It also stocks hardware such as buckles, toggles, zippers, hook-and-loop fasteners, cams, and grommets, and can source additional components as needed. Customers range from small-scale custom orders to larger manufacturing programs.

Mammoth Manufacturing emphasizes its 30-plus years of experience, versatile capabilities, rigorous quality control, and a customer-oriented approach as key differentiators. The business originated from Rodgers' own need for better hardware, a problem-solving mindset that continues to guide its project consultations today.

Rigorous quality control measures on every product

name: Manufacture Good
old_description: At Manufacture Good, we integrate meaningful workforce development experience with both personal and spiritual growth. The young men that come into our program are improving their lives by learning how to serve as a highly skilled tradesmen and as thoughtful community members. To cultivate workforce talent, apprentices support the production of custom furniture which is designed and made right here in our local Birmingham woodshop.
about:
Manufacture Good, originally founded as Magic City Woodworks in 2013, operates from a training campus in downtown Birmingham, Alabama. The organization began in a borrowed one-car garage in nearby Hoover when founder Lawrence Sheffield launched a grassroots effort to teach woodworking trades to young men alongside spiritual mentorship. The Lawson family provided the initial workspace, and within a year the program outgrew the space, eventually receiving a donated commercial warehouse from the Cathey family that enabled expansion into a dedicated facility.

The company produces handcrafted furniture including tables, desks, seating, shelves, and custom cabinetry, all designed and built by apprentices in the Birmingham woodshop. A master craftsman team oversees production, which also includes a firewood operation that cuts, splits, seasons, delivers, and stacks wood for customers. The apprenticeship program pays participants while they learn woodworking and life skills, with the workshop serving as both a production floor and a training ground.

Finished pieces are sold to residential clients, churches, and businesses nationwide, while the firewood service delivers directly to local customers. The apprentice cohort—typically young men seeking trade skills and personal development—forms the core labor force, supported by mentors, shop staff, and an executive team that includes an executive director, operations director, and apprenticeship foreman. A board of directors drawn from local construction, finance, and healthcare sectors provides governance.

Sheffield has stated that the enterprise was started to create a workshop where young men could come to faith while developing the hands and minds needed to provide for themselves and their families. The organization describes its model as “making disciples while making good things,” using product revenue and donor support to sustain a ministry that aims to prepare participants for roles as husbands, fathers, craftsmen, and community leaders.

name: Manufacturing Solutions, Inc. (MSI)
old_description: Durable, high-quality finishes with scalable capacity—powered by advanced automation and built for consistency. From prototyping to production runs, we deliver reliable coating solutions that enhance performance, appearance, and long-term durability.
about:
Manufacturing Solutions, Inc. (MSI) was founded in 1996 by Garret Hirchak in Morrisville, Vermont. Hirchak serves as CEO, and Bethany Salvas has been president since the company's inception. The business began as a contract manufacturing operation focused on bringing product ideas to reality through fabrication, assembly, and finishing services.

Today MSI operates a vertically integrated facility in Morrisville offering CNC machining (milling and turning), sheet metal fabrication, welding, automated powder coating on a Gema SMART Series line, 3D printing, and both electrical and mechanical assembly. The company also provides fulfillment services including picking, kitting, packing, warehousing, and third‑party logistics, allowing it to manage projects from prototype through high‑volume production and delivery.

MSI serves original equipment manufacturers and other businesses requiring precision metal parts, coated finishes, and full supply‑chain support. Its NAICS codes span machine shops, sheet metal work, fabricated metal products, and warehousing, though the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals or named customers.

The company emphasizes a vertically integrated model—keeping equipment, team, and processes under one roof—to improve communication, speed, and quality control. Founder Garret Hirchak has stated that the goal is to “competitively manufacture products in the USA,” and the leadership team cites values such as accountability, flexibility, and collaboration as cultural differentiators.

name: Marchel Industries
old_description: Marchel Industries is a full service plastic injection molding and machining facility located in Spartanburg, SC. Our 35,000 square foot climate controlled facility is equipped with state of the art injection molding and CNC machining equipment and is ready to take on your 20 – 400 ton press injection molding project. In addition to full service plastic injection molding, our capabilities include precision machining, EDM machining, plastic design, custom molding, reverse engineering, prototyping, parts assembly, testing, and dimensional analysis. ISO 9001:2015 certified, we are committed to quality and excellent customer service in all industries that we serve, including OEM, medical, government, military and industrial. Contact us today for a quote on your next injection molding or machining project.
about:
Marchel Industries was founded in 1992 in Spartanburg, South Carolina, as an American-based precision injection molding and manufacturing company. In February 2023 the business was acquired by Plastifab, a extrusion firm, to create a complete plastics partner offering both extrusion and injection molding services.

The company operates a 35,000-square-foot climate-controlled facility equipped with 20- to 400-ton injection molding presses, CNC machining centers, and EDM equipment. Its capabilities span plastic injection molding, precision machining, EDM machining, plastic design, custom molding, reverse engineering, prototyping, parts assembly, testing, and dimensional analysis. The firm also provides project management from design through manufacturing and delivery.

Marchel serves OEMs, medical, government, military, industrial, and telecommunications sectors. It handles both high-volume OEM production and short-run concept modeling projects.

The company emphasizes Lean Manufacturing principles, ISO 9001:2015 certification, in-house design and machining, and a goal of zero defects. It aims to be the "Plastic Injection Molded Part Vendor of Choice" through Southern hospitality, high-quality manufacturing, and state-of-the-art technology.

name: Mark Downs Office Furniture
old_description: Since 1933, Mark Downs Office Furniture has been the preferred source for discount office furniture in Maryland. Businesses have been coming to us to help address their office cubicles and space planning needs.  Whether fitting more people in an existing space, laying out a new office, or re-configuring a current layout, businesses come to us to help design a winning environment and achieve their goals.
about:
Mark Downs Office Furniture has operated from Towson, Maryland since 1933, making it one of the region's longest-standing office furniture retailers. The company maintains a 10,000-square-foot showroom on Gleneagles Court that displays one of the largest office furniture selections in the state.

The business sells new, remanufactured, and used office furniture across categories including cubicles, desks, seating, filing and storage, tables, and accessories. It partners with multiple manufacturers — among them Steelcase and N9NE Furniture Group — to stock a range of price points. In addition to product sales, Mark Downs provides complimentary space planning and design services, using 3D rendering software to develop floor plans and furniture recommendations for projects of any size.

Customers span corporate offices, call centers, healthcare practices, and home offices throughout the Baltimore–Washington corridor. Reviews cite engagements ranging from a 25-year call-center buyer outfitting a large center to a small therapy suite needing only a few pieces. The company also serves residential buyers seeking single items such as ergonomic chairs.

Mark Downs positions its value on decades of product knowledge and a consultative approach: the team evaluates each environment, develops layouts, and assembles furniture before delivery. The model combines a physical showroom experience with design expertise that the company says removes the guesswork from fitting workstations into a given footprint.

name: Martin Bamberger Co
old_description: “ I have been in business since 1995 and my company was fortunate enough to meet Henry Bamberger and his company from the get go. They have been excellent and punctual with our supplies and services. Whenever we have a problem with any of our equipment, they are right there on time to fix it, so we can take care of our own customers. They have been invaluable to our business and I consider our business lucky to have them on board and highly recommend them. ”
about:
Martin Bamberger Company operates from Baltimore, Maryland, tracing its roots to 1942 when Martin Bamberger opened a small shop supplying grocery stores. Three generations later, the business remains family-owned and operated, having grown from a local supplier into a multi-state distributor of commercial food service equipment.

The company stocks and sells a broad inventory of new and reconditioned equipment, including refrigeration units (walk-ins, reach-ins, sandwich prep tables), cooking appliances, and meat-processing machinery. Beyond sales, it provides installation, preventive maintenance, and emergency repair services for commercial kitchens. The firm reports having serviced hundreds of kitchens and sold thousands of products across five states.

Its customer base spans grocery stores, supermarkets, bakeries, cafés, butcher shops, restaurants, cafeterias, healthcare facilities, houses of worship, and educational institutions. Long-term clients cited by the company include Graul's Markets, Klein's ShopRite, The Artisan Butcher, Cube Coffee, Di Pasquale Italian Gourmet, The Food Market, Miller's Food Market, and Annapolis Area Christian School.

The business emphasizes continuity and personal service: multi-generational family ownership, prompt on-site repair response, and involvement from kitchen design through installation and follow-up. These traits are presented as the foundation of its decades-long relationships with independent food retailers and operators.

name: Martin Steel Inc.
old_description: Martin Steel, Inc. has been in the business of steel processing and fabrication since 1952 and has experienced supervisory and management personnel with the expertise to maintain our excellent reputation for quality workmanship and meeting schedules. We are constantly striving to improve our services and products to better serve our customers.
about:
Martin Steel, Inc. has operated from Huntington, West Virginia since 1952. The company began as a steel processing and fabrication business and has grown to a 125,800-square-foot facility with 85,800 square feet under roof and 40,000 square feet of outdoor storage. No founders are named in available sources, and ownership structure is not publicly disclosed.

The firm provides structural, miscellaneous, and specialty steel fabrication, including CNC plasma cutting, laser punching, bending, rolling, welding, piping, and plate work. Its two-building complex houses five bays equipped with robotics and computerized machinery, enabling large-capacity projects. The company also offers design and drafting services. Headcount and annual volume are not published.

Martin Steel serves a broad industrial base across the United States, with a regional focus on the Huntington–Ironton–Ashland tri-state area. Customers include aircraft production facilities, chemical plants, power plants, oil refineries, pharmaceutical facilities, bridges, railroads, mining operations, water purification plants, and government construction projects. The company ships via highway, rail, and Ohio River barge access.

The company emphasizes systematic, thorough operations and a full-time skilled workforce that coordinates, manages, and inspects each project to stringent quality standards. It cites its experienced supervisory personnel and adaptive, flexible processes as key differentiators.

about:
Martin's Equipment, Inc. operates from Statesville, North Carolina, and has served the region since its founding in 1996. The company sells new and used commercial restaurant equipment to both the public and industry professionals across North Carolina and surrounding states.

The company stocks a broad range of commercial kitchen categories including ice machines, refrigeration, cooking equipment, dishwashing and sanitation, food preparation, and dining room supplies. In addition to sales, Martin's Equipment purchases used restaurant equipment — from single items to entire kitchen liquidations — and handles removal and transport. New and used inventory arrives daily at their physical location, which is open Monday through Friday.

Customers range from independent restaurant owners and chefs to institutional food-service operators throughout North Carolina and neighboring states. The company works with anyone needing commercial kitchen equipment, whether outfitting a new location, replacing a single fryer, or clearing out a closing establishment.

Martin's Equipment emphasizes competitive pricing on both new and used inventory, and promotes its ability to complete most liquidations within the seller's required timeframe using its own removal equipment and transport.

name: Mass Renewables
old_description: Mike Kelley is co-owner of Mass Renewables Inc. and lives in Bellingham with his wife Kathy and three daughters. He is a life-long resident of Massachusetts and has been in the solar business since 2009. Mike has been certified by the North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners as an “NABCEP PV Installer” which is the most prestigious certification for solar professionals. Mike was drawn to solar energy because of the fact that we already have the technology in place, the incentives available, and the endless source of pollution-free energy every day when the sun rises.
about:
Mass Renewables is based in Bellingham, Massachusetts, and was founded in 2009 by Mike Kelley and Jeff Herman. The two co-owners — whose wives are sisters — run the company as a family business. Kelley, a lifelong Massachusetts resident, entered the solar industry in 2009 and holds NABCEP PV Installer certification. Herman brought three decades of construction experience, spanning residential remodeling to large-scale commercial projects, and serves as project manager.

The firm designs and installs residential and commercial photovoltaic systems, including AllEarth Renewables dual-axis trackers and Tesla Powerwall battery storage. It also offers financing options (purchase or lease), 24/7 system monitoring, proactive service dispatch, and full maintenance coverage. The installation crew comprises NABCEP-certified and OSHA-certified professionals, master electricians, and licensed builders. Since opening in 2009, the company has served customers across Massachusetts.

Mass Renewables works with homeowners seeking to reduce electric bills and businesses aiming to meet sustainability targets. Reference clients include residential customers such as Jonathan DeKock, who added Powerwalls to an existing array, and commercial accounts that use tracker systems to maximize production. The company emphasizes local expertise in Massachusetts incentives, including the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard.

The founders frame the business around energy independence and carbon reduction. Kelley was drawn to solar because the technology, incentives, and a pollution-free energy source already exist. Herman’s goal is to adapt the technology so the company outlives government incentives and continues serving the region for decades. A production guarantee — “Energy Guaranteed or we pay you” — underscores the performance commitment.
